notes:
Lead source: organic inbound via blog post on classroom copilots.

Quick summary: small K-12 focused startup building teacher/student assistant that ingests lesson plans, student submissions, and classroom chat. Primary asks: robust moderation, low cost per token, teacher-facing control over memory/retention. They are comfortable with hosted API if residency + retention controls are clear.

Tech/eval notes:
- Tried hosted API with free credits; created API key and ran small POC (2k queries across sample lessons).
- Embeddings for search: recall good for short queries; want advice on index refresh cadence.
- Chat copilot latency target: ~200ms p95 for short prompts; acceptable up to 300ms for more complex context windows.
- Moderation: require profanity and PII detection, automated removal of student identifiers in responses. Called out FERPA specifically.
- Cost sensitivity: founder repeated "budget is tight — want to keep infra <$1.5k/mo"; asked about smaller open models, 8-bit quant, and batching suggestions.
- Data retention: want configurable retention per student (30/90/365 days) and easy purge API.

Sales/ops notes:
- Interested in hosted_api (self-serve) but will need security answers before to proceed. SE (Marcus) recommended prefix caching + intelligent batching to cut token spend. Suggested Optimize plays for quantization recommendations.
- Legal wants explicit statement on student data residency (US-only) — we shared security FAQ but need to escalate for residency confirmation.

Quotes: "We need a copilot teachers can trust — no hallucinations, and student data must be private." — Maya Lopez, CTO

Open actions: send short FERPA-specific FAQ, provide example retention/purge API snippet, price two options (pay-as-you-go vs monthly cap with burst). Schedule 30m follow-up 2026-03-12.
notes_short: SMB K-12 edtech inbound. Moderation + copilot. Budget constrained; FERPA/residency are main blockers.
